content.title: Plan: agt events namespace (list/add) + custom event type design
content.description: Design the new `agt events` CLI namespace and the library API backing it. Scope: (1) New CLI namespace replacing `agt history <issueId>` with `agt events list <issueId>`; add `--type <event-type>` filter flag. (2) New `agt events add <issueId> <event-json>` command accepting a JSON object with `type` and `content` (content is an arbitrary JSON object); agentrack auto-attaches `timestamp` and `author`. (3) Define the set of agentrack default/reserved event types and the validation rule that custom event `type` MUST NOT collide with them. (4) Tracker API methods (e.g. eventsList / eventsAdd) and resulting type changes. (6) Migration/deprecation note for the removed `agt history` command. Produce a spec for the library-developer.

content.content:
# Spec: agt events namespace, list and add commands plus custom event types

## Goal
Replace the agt history command with a richer agt events namespace that lists raw events with optional type filtering, and lets agents or humans append arbitrary, validated custom events to an issue event log. Custom events are stored alongside reserved agentrack events but are never interpreted by agentrack state computation.

## Scope
In scope: the event types module, the core events module, the tracker module, the errors module, the api types module, the types index barrel, the library index barrel, a new cli events commands module, and the cli runner module.
Out of scope: webapp, mentions, push and pull.

---

## 1. Event model changes, in the event types module

### 1.1 New CustomEvent variant
Add a new event variant representing user or agent-authored events. The type field is a caller-chosen string that must not collide with a reserved type. The content field is an arbitrary JSON object, plain object only, not array or primitive.

    export interface CustomEvent extends BaseEvent {
      type: string;
      content: Record<string, unknown>;
    }

Update the Event union to include CustomEvent.

Discrimination note: the reserved variants have string-literal type fields; CustomEvent widens type to string. Existing switch-on-type and equality checks in the core events module continue to work unchanged because they test against the specific literals first and fall through for unknown or custom types. Do NOT add any default branch that throws. Custom events must be silently ignored by computeState and computeComments, which is already the case today.

### 1.2 Reserved event types registry
Export a frozen list and helper. The list contains creation, update, comment, comment-update, comment-delete, blockage-added, blockage-resolved, blockage-deleted.

    export const RESERVED_EVENT_TYPES = [
      "creation", "update", "comment", "comment-update", "comment-delete",
      "blockage-added", "blockage-resolved", "blockage-deleted",
    ] as const;

    export type ReservedEventType = (typeof RESERVED_EVENT_TYPES)[number];

    export function isReservedEventType(type: string): boolean {
      return (RESERVED_EVENT_TYPES as readonly string[]).includes(type);
    }

Re-export RESERVED_EVENT_TYPES, ReservedEventType, isReservedEventType, and CustomEvent from the types index barrel and the library index barrel.

---

## 2. Core computation, in the core events module
No behavioral change required. Confirm by tests that:
- A CustomEvent appended to an issue file does NOT alter computeState output for title, status, assignee, tags, priority, parentId.
- A CustomEvent does NOT appear in computeComments.
- updatedAt in computeState SHOULD reflect the custom event timestamp, since it already keys off the last event timestamp. Keep this; custom events are real activity and bumping updatedAt is correct.

---

## 3. Error code, in the errors module
Add one new code: RESERVED_EVENT_TYPE with result RESERVED_EVENT_TYPE and exitCode 22. Reuse existing INVALID_PARAMS, exitCode 10, for malformed payload: non-object content, missing or empty type, bad JSON.

---

## 4. Tracker API, in the tracker module and api types module

### 4.1 New types in the api types module
EventsListParams has an optional type field for an exact-match type filter, reserved or custom. EventsListResult is Event array or AgentrackError. EventsAddParams has a caller-chosen type string that must not be reserved, a content JSON object payload, and an optional author override resolved by the auth layer. EventsAddResult is result OK or AgentrackError.

    export interface EventsListParams {
      type?: string;
    }
    export type EventsListResult = Event[] | AgentrackError;

    export interface EventsAddParams {
      type: string;
      content: Record<string, unknown>;
      author?: string;
    }
    export type EventsAddResult = { result: "OK" } | AgentrackError;

Keep the existing HistoryResult type but mark deprecated in a JSDoc comment; alias it to EventsListResult for back-compat. Re-export the new types from the types index barrel and the library index barrel.

### 4.2 Tracker methods
Replace the existing history id method with two methods: eventsList and eventsAdd.

    async eventsList(id: IssueId, params: EventsListParams = {}): Promise<EventsListResult>;
    async eventsAdd(id: IssueId, params: EventsAddParams): Promise<EventsAddResult>;

eventsList: same auth, index, and missing-file checks as the current history method. After replayEvents on the issue file path, if params.type is defined, filter the result to events whose type equals params.type. Return the possibly-filtered array.

eventsAdd flow:
1. resolveTrackerDir, NOT_INITIALIZED if missing; auth requiresWrite true since it mutates.
2. Resolve author via resolveAuthor; throw on AgentrackError.
3. readIndex then findEntry; throw NOT_FOUND if absent.
4. Build issue file path from entry path; throw ISSUE_MISSING if the file does not exist.
5. Validate. params.type must be a non-empty string after trim, else AgentrackError INVALID_PARAMS with message about non-empty type and exit 10. If isReservedEventType params.type is true, AgentrackError RESERVED_EVENT_TYPE with a message naming the reserved type and exit 22. params.content must be a plain object: typeof object, not null, not Array; reject arrays and primitives as INVALID_PARAMS.
6. Construct the CustomEvent with type params.type, content params.content, timestamp from new Date toISOString, and the resolved author.
7. await appendEvent on the issue file path with the event.
8. Return result OK.

Back-compat alias: keep a deprecated async history id returning HistoryResult that delegates to this.eventsList id. Add a deprecated JSDoc pointing to eventsList.

---

## 5. CLI namespace, new cli events commands module and the cli runner module

### 5.1 New cli events commands module
Two handlers, following the exact try-catch plus writeStdout, writeStderr, and process exit pattern used in the comments command module.

    export async function eventsListAction(issueId: string, options: { type?: string }): Promise<void>;
    export async function eventsAddAction(issueId: string, eventJson: string): Promise<void>;

eventsListAction calls tracker.eventsList(issueId, options.type present with type options.type else empty object).

eventsAddAction flow:
1. Parse eventJson with JSON.parse. On SyntaxError, write INVALID_PARAMS with a message to stderr and exit 10.
2. Validate the parsed value is a plain object with a type string and a content object, mirroring tracker rules for early friendly CLI errors. The tracker remains the source of truth and MUST re-validate.
3. Call tracker.eventsAdd(issueId, an object with type parsed.type and content parsed.content).
4. Handle AgentrackError including RESERVED_EVENT_TYPE exit 22 and success, like the other commands.

### 5.2 Wire into the cli runner module
- Remove the historyAction import and the program.command history issueId block.
- Add an import of eventsAddAction and eventsListAction from the new events commands module.
- Register the namespace with a top-level events command, a list subcommand taking issueId with an optional type flag, and an add subcommand taking issueId and an event-json argument.
- Delete the old history command module, no longer referenced.

---

## 6. Acceptance criteria
1. agt events list issueId returns the same JSON array agt history issueId returned previously.
2. agt events list issueId with type comment returns only events whose type equals comment.
3. agt events add issueId with type label.added and content label bug appends a CustomEvent; a subsequent agt view issueId shows updatedAt bumped, but NO change to title, status, assignee, tags, priority, parentId, or comments.
4. agt events add issueId with type creation exits 22 with result RESERVED_EVENT_TYPE. Same for every type in RESERVED_EVENT_TYPES.
5. agt events add issueId with type x and no content, and agt events add issueId with invalid json, exit 10 with INVALID_PARAMS.
6. agt history issueId is no longer recognized; commander unknown-command behavior is fine, no crash.
7. tracker.eventsList id with type filter and tracker.eventsAdd id with params work from the TS API; tracker.history id still works, deprecated, returns the unfiltered list.
8. Custom events round-trip through replayEvents and eventsList with identical type, content, timestamp, author.
9. Existing tests for computeState, computeComments, and history still pass; tracker.history users see no regression.

---

## 7. Tests to add, library
- eventsList returns full list with no filter; returns filtered subset with type.
- eventsAdd success appends a CustomEvent read back via replayEvents; updatedAt bumps; computed state otherwise unchanged; comments unchanged.
- eventsAdd rejects reserved type exit 22, rejects missing or non-string type, rejects array or primitive content, rejects when issue missing, not-found, or not-initialized.
- eventsAdd resolves author from auth layer and stamps ISO timestamp.
- CLI: events add with invalid JSON exits 10; reserved type exits 22; success exits 0 and writes the appended event.
- Update any existing test that invoked agt history to use agt events list.

## 8. Migration and deprecation note
The agt history issueId CLI command is REMOVED, not aliased, because the new namespace is a strict superset. Library consumers using tracker.history id keep working via a deprecated alias that delegates to eventsList. Upgrade guidance:
- CLI: agt history id becomes agt events list id. Drop type for the old unfiltered behavior.
- To view only a certain activity: agt events list id with type update.
- To record custom activity: agt events add id with type your.type and a content object. Reserved types — creation, update, comment, comment-update, comment-delete, blockage-added, blockage-resolved, blockage-deleted — are rejected; pick a namespaced type like label.added or review.requested.

## 9. Non-goals and future
- No CLI time-range filters; can be added later as additional EventsListParams.
- No update or delete of custom events; append-only model preserved.
- No cross-issue indexing of custom event types.

Spec complete. Summary for PM: I designed the agt events namespace to replace agt history. Key decisions: (1) introduce a CustomEvent variant in the event union with a caller-chosen string type and an arbitrary JSON content object; (2) define a RESERVED_EVENT_TYPES registry of the 8 existing agentrack types plus an isReservedEventType helper; (3) add a new error code RESERVED_EVENT_TYPE (exit 22) for collisions, reusing INVALID_PARAMS (exit 10) for malformed payloads; (4) add tracker.eventsList with optional type filter and tracker.eventsAdd with server-side validation, auto-stamping timestamp and author; (5) keep tracker.history as a deprecated back-compat alias delegating to eventsList so library consumers are unaffected; (6) remove the agt history CLI command entirely in favor of agt events list with a type flag and agt events add. Custom events are ignored by computeState and computeComments but DO bump updatedAt. The full implementable spec is in the previous comment and is detailed enough for the library-developer (mqgxdt9me7) to implement. Marking this planning task done so the implementation task is unblocked.
